summary:
Kocaeli is a province of Turkey and stands under the national framework set out for the country. No statute, court decision, enforcement incident or provincial documentation specific to Kocaeli appears in the sources, so the assessment below describes the national regime a visitor to Kocaeli is subject to.

A leaked omnibus draft, the 11th Judicial Package, reported by Human Rights Watch on 29 October 2025, would amend the penal code to criminalise conduct deemed contrary to biological sex and general morality with up to three years' prison, and participation in same-sex engagement or marriage ceremonies with up to four years. The same draft would raise the minimum age for gender-affirming care, including surgery, from 18 to 25, with mandatory permanent infertility and repeated evaluations at government-approved hospitals. Healthcare professionals performing such interventions would face fines and up to seven years in prison, and trans people receiving care deemed illegal up to three years. Human Rights Watch warns the package would force treatment underground and expose people to arrest and pretrial detention. Fifteen LGBT groups and the Turkish Medical Association opposed the draft.

Hostility toward LGBTI+ people has become explicit state policy, according to Kaos GL's 2025 monitoring review. Public institutions received "Year of the Family" instructions, an LGBTI+ association was closed with criminal cases opened against 11 of its members, and artistic events were cancelled or banned.

Kaos GL recorded roughly 313 violations in 2025, about two and a half times the previous year's total, alongside 299 detention decisions. Six violations of the right to life were recorded, three of them hate-motivated killings, with trans people the most affected group. Torture and ill-treatment violations rose to 89 from 51 the prior year, and freedom-of-expression violations rose from 216 to 540.
tangentialFactors:
The draft package's restrictions on gender-affirming care would apply nationwide, including in Kocaeli, and would narrow an already restricted route to transition-related treatment rather than create a new prohibition specific to the province.

Kocaeli adjoins Istanbul, where street-level enforcement against trans women has been documented: stops for background checks at which foreigners are required to produce original identity documents. No equivalent Kocaeli-specific stop pattern is sourced here, but the document-carry requirement applies at transit checkpoints across Turkey, and any such interaction occasions comparison between presentation and passport gender marker.

The rise in recorded detention decisions and freedom-of-expression violations country-wide in 2025 indicates an enforcement tempo that a visitor may encounter at demonstrations, venues and checkpoints regardless of province.
localsOnly:
Residents of Kocaeli face the same national criminal-law exposure as the rest of the country: the pending draft package's penalties for conduct deemed contrary to biological sex and general morality, and for participation in same-sex ceremonies, would bind locally if enacted.

Organisational space is constricted nationwide. Kaos GL records an LGBTI+ association closed with criminal cases against 11 members, artistic events cancelled or banned, and "Year of the Family" instructions issued to public institutions, all of which bear on residents' participation in community life in Kocaeli.

Freedom-of-expression violations rose from 216 to 540 in 2025, and torture and ill-treatment violations rose from 51 to 89, indicating heightened exposure for residents who are stopped, detained or publicly visible.

The draft package would raise the age threshold for gender-affirming care to 25 with mandatory permanent infertility and repeated evaluations at government-approved hospitals, and would penalise providers with up to seven years' prison, conditions that shape what care a resident can seek and from whom.
outOfScopeNotes:
No Kocaeli-specific statute, provincial circular, enforcement incident, Pride event record or detention record appears in the available sources; every substantive claim here is national-framework and applies to Kocaeli by extension.

The 11th Judicial Package was a leaked draft as of 29 October 2025. Whether it has since been tabled, amended or enacted is unresolved in the sources.

Whether Kocaeli police conduct document-check stops of the kind documented in Istanbul is not sourced; the national original-identification requirement at checkpoints is documented, the local stop pattern is not.

Provincial health-directorate practice in Kocaeli on transition-related referrals, and whether any Kocaeli facility is designated for the evaluations the draft would require, are not sourced.
